title: Pest Control Company License Database
demand_signal: Strong and validated. 8+ commercial vendors selling pest control company databases: Openmart (25K+ companies, 97% accuracy), Prospeo.io (116,683 companies with 483,409 contacts), LimeLeads (92% accuracy, 90-day refresh), FacilityManagementLeads (300K+ contacts), DataCaptive (12K+ companies), Coldlytics, AverickMedia, Bancomail (5,665 records). The pest control software market alone is valued at $431.55M in 2026, confirming strong vendor ecosystem selling into this vertical.
target_audience: Pest control field service management software vendors (PestPac, Jobber, Briostack, PestRoutes, ServSuite, Pocomos) running customer acquisition campaigns; chemical and pesticide manufacturers/distributors (Rentokil, Rollins/Orkin supply chain); pest control franchise development teams (Terminix, Orkin, ABC Home & Commercial); commercial property managers seeking pest control vendor bids; pest control insurance brokers (general liability, workers comp); pest control industry associations (NPMA) for membership drives; fleet/vehicle leasing companies targeting service vehicle operators
public_data_sources: Texas Department of Agriculture — Structural Pest Control Reports: Current Licenses (downloadable)
California Structural Pest Control Board — license search portal (no auth required)
Florida FDACS — public license search and verification (aeslicensing.fdacs.gov)
North Carolina Department of Agriculture — Structural Pest Control license search
Georgia Department of Agriculture — search licenses portal
Washington State Department of Agriculture — license and company portals
Illinois DOH Environmental — pest control business verification search
New York DEC Bureau of Pesticides Management — business and applicator search
competitive_landscape: Moderately crowded at premium tier. Openmart and Prospeo have the largest databases (25K-116K companies). General B2B providers (LimeLeads, DataCaptive, FacilityManagementLeads) include pest control as a category. No vendor offers clean, one-time state-level CSVs from verified state licensing boards at a flat price. All use subscription or per-contact pricing. DataStructured wedge: $39-$49 per state CSV sourced directly from state agriculture department licensing registries — public data, verifiable, compliance-safe.
monetization_model: State-level CSVs at $39-$49 each. Fields: business name, license holder name, license number, license type (structural pest control, termite, fumigation), license status, issue/expiration dates, business address, phone. Start with TX (large market, downloadable data), CA, FL. Multi-state bundle: 'Top 10 States Pest Control Licenses' at $149. Target: PestPac and Jobber sales teams who run state-by-state territory campaigns.
estimated_market_size: 25,000-120,000 pest control companies in the US (range depends on counting method — licensed operators vs. businesses). 68% use at least one software tool (2024 data). $431M pest control software market growing at 8.7% CAGR. Buyer LTV: field service software $50-$500/month ($600-$6,000/year), chemical supply contracts $5,000-$50,000/year, franchise fees $50K-$150K upfront.
data_freshness_requirement: Annual updates aligned with state license renewal cycles. Most states require annual or biennial renewal. Texas publishes current license reports that can be harvested periodically.
compliance_notes: PASS potential: All data sourced from state agriculture department and structural pest control board public licensing registries. License information is public record intended for consumer protection — consumers can verify if their pest control provider is properly licensed. No PII beyond business owner/licensee names (already public record). Source attribution via state agency URLs.
next_steps: Harvest Texas Dept of Agriculture structural pest control license reports (downloadable format confirmed)
Harvest California Structural Pest Control Board via license search scraping
Harvest Florida FDACS pest control business licenses
Clean and standardize across states into unified CSV schema
Launch TX as first SKU at $39 on Gumroad, target r/pestcontrol and LinkedIn pest control industry groups
researcher_notes: Solid opportunity with excellent public data availability. The key advantage is that pest control is a state-licensed occupation in all 50 states via agriculture departments and structural pest control boards — unlike many other trades, there's a clear licensing authority with public records in every state. Texas even publishes downloadable reports. Engineering complexity is low-to-moderate: 8 states with confirmed public portals, most with searchable interfaces. The $431M software market (PestPac, Jobber, Briostack) means strong buyer LTV and recurring demand from SaaS sales teams running territory expansions. Not as high-scoring as auto dealerships or self-storage because buyer LTV is lower and the niche is narrower, but the public data access is among the best of any opportunity in our pipeline.
